title: Elements with Attachments

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: ### What problem are you trying to solve? What if, in addition to being capable of having child nodes and attributes, DOM elements could have attachments? Creating a means for elements to have attachments would enable or simplify new approaches to a number of challenges such as [accessibility](https://www.w3.org/mission/accessibility/) and [internationalization](https://www.w3.org/mission/internationalization/). ### What solutions exist today? With respect to Web accessibility, solutions exist today such as placing [ARIA attributes](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/aria/) on documents' elements. ### How would you solve it? I would first consider adding to the [`Element`](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element) interface in a manner resembling: ```webidl partial interface Element { AttachmentList getAttachments(DOMString qualifiedName, optional object options); AttachmentList getAttachmentsNS(DOMString namespace, DOMString localName, optional object options); undefined setAttachments(DOMString qualifiedName, AttachmentList attachments); undefined setAttachmentsNS(DOMString namespace, DOMString localName, AttachmentList attachments); boolean hasAttachments(DOMString qualifiedName, optional object options); boolean hasAttachmentsNS(DOMString namespace, DOMString localName, optional object options); } ``` ### Anything else? One means of declaring attachments would be to create a new `` tag for defining individual attachments, e.g., in documents' `` sections, and also a new `` metadata tag – adding to `` and `` – to specify which elements to attach attachments to. ```html This is hypertext to be attached to a picture below. ``` ```js document.getElementById('p1').getAttachments('aria-description'); ``` Perhaps multiple attachments could be specified with varying content types. ```html This is hypertext to be attached to a picture below. This is hypertext to be attached to a picture below. ``` ```js document.getElementById('p1').getAttachments('aria-description', { type: 'application/ssml+xml' }); ``` Perhaps internationalization scenarios could be supported. ```html This is hypertext to be attached to a picture below. Ceci est hypertexte à associer à une image ci-dessous. ``` ```js document.getElementById('p1').getAttachments('aria-description', { lang: 'en' }); ``` Perhaps attachments, additionally or instead, could be inline resources: ```html This is hypertext to be attached to a picture below. Ceci est hypertexte à associer à une image ci-dessous. ``` Perhaps attachments could be remote resources: ```html ``` Using [RFC 2392](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2392), one could use the `mid:` or `cid:` URL schemes to reference other parts of multipart MIME messages. ```html ``` Perhaps, in addition to having a `name` attribute, `` elements could have a `rel` attribute. Then, one could select attachments by `name` and, optionally, by using `rel`. ```html ``` ```js document.getElementById('p1').getAttachments(null, { rel: 'accessibility', lang: 'en' }); ``` Interestingly, one could also use attachments to implement a kind of proxy pattern. For the proxy pattern, attached markup content would be available to replace that element which has the attachment. Using it, one could make another `` element, `
